articles.title: Cong hails launch of India's imaging satellite - MillenniumPost
articles.content: Cong hails launch of India’s imaging satellite By - Team MP Update: 2026-09-04 18:39 GMT New Delh,: The Congress on Friday hailed ISRO for the successful launch of the country’s first-ever imaging satellite in geo-orbit and accused the Modi government of undertaking a “radical role reconfiguration” that will “change the very character” of the Indian space agency. The Opposition party said the launch would also undoubtedly be a big morale booster to the space agency “since it has found itself under attack from various quarters”. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on Friday made its way into history books yet again with the successful launch of the country’s first ever imaging satellite in geo-orbit, placing the over 2,300 kg payload into a precise orbit using a GSLV rocket. Friday’s launch marked the space agency’s maiden success for the year 2026. In a post on X, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said, “Congratulations to the entire @isro team on the successful GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission! EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite, from Geosynchronous orbit, will further strengthen our Earth Observation capabilities that we have been developing for years.” “We are immensely proud of our scientists, space engineers and researchers whose dedication and ingenuity continue to take India’s space programme to greater heights,” the Congress chief said. The Congress party has always remained deeply committed to scientific temper and space research, he said.

articles.title: ISRO successfully deploys India's first geosynchronous imaging satellite into orbit - Public TV English
articles.content: SRIHARIKOTA (Andhra Pradesh): The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully deployed the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday, marking another major milestone in India’s space programme. ISRO chief V Narayanan on Friday announced that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05), the geo-imaging star satellite, into its intended and required orbit. The launch took place from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, SHAR. The launch was carried on a GSLV-F17 rocket which is the 19th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) as it EOS-05 towards a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (Sub-GTO). 🚀𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚 𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐚 𝐦𝐚𝐣𝐨𝐫 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐬𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐡𝐧𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐲! ISRO’s state-of-the-art Earth observation satellite EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit, was successfully launched aboard a GSLV rocket from… pic.twitter.com/jqdQ9bsEyt — All India Radio News (@airnewsalerts) September 4, 2026 Narayanan said the successful mission was a significant achievement for India’s space programme and that the satellite’s health was perfectly alright after its injection into orbit. “I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite 05, the geo-imaging satellite, in the intended and required orbit,” Narayanan said right after the mission success was announced at the space center. More Read Victory for BJP’s fight, says LoP R Ashoka after Congress govt withdraws bill 5 pc park land use Indian markets open higher on private capex optimism despite rising crude prices He added that once EOS-05 is operationalised in orbit, it will become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite from the geo orbit and provide important strategic data for the country. “Today, we have injected the heaviest satellite, 2367 kgs, using this launch vehicle. The health of the satellite is perfectly alright,” the ISRO chief said. Narayanan credited the successful mission to the collective efforts of the entire ISRO team, along with its industrial partners and the academic community. “This success is the culmination of the hard work of the entire ISRO team along with our industrial partners and academia. On this occasion, I congratulate each and every one of you. This is a great achievement in our country’s space programme,” he said. #WATCH | Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh: ISRO Chief V Narayanan says, “I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite 05, the geo-imaging star satellite, in the intended and required orbit…… pic.twitter.com/bW6mHJ3wzL — ANI (@ANI) September 3, 2026 Praising the ISRO and scientists involved in the mission, Minister of State in Department of Space, Jitendra Singh wrote on X, “Another giant leap for India in Space! Kudos to Team @isro on the successful launch of GSLV-F17/EOS-05. EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth Observation satellite and India’s first imaging satellite from Geosynchronous Orbit, enabling advanced imaging across visible, infrared, multi-spectral and hyperspectral bands. articles.title: India's First 'Sentient' Corporate Campus to Come in Pune - Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Mumbai: India’s first sentient corporate campus will be set up at Bajaj FinservCampus at Koregaon Park Annexe, Pune. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday laid the foundation stone for the project. Speaking at the ceremony, CM Fadnavis said that the Bajaj Finserv Campus will not only be the largest but also the most intelligent and sustainable ecosystem in the country. Built with AI and IOT at its core, the Bajaj FinservCampus building will sense its environment and occupants’ needs and proactively adapt in real time. According to company sources, the AI and IoT systems will enable the Campus to respond to changing weather, occupancy and environmental conditions. Sensors and analytics will help optimise energy and water consumption, crowd density and movement. Predictive maintenance systems using IoT sensors will monitor critical infrastructure, while automation and robotics will support Campus operations. The Campus’ eco-efficient design will maximise natural breeze and daylight while reducing cooling requirements. The Campus will operate on renewable energy and target 80% water recycling, rainwater harvesting and zero waste. It’s biophilic design will bring nature into the workplace through extensive green zones, including rare Ayurvedic gardens, Miyawaki and replanted native forests. Native species from Maharashtra will be used to support biodiversity. The Campus will be supported by floor and cluster-level monitoring of air quality and temperature. An integrated employee app will provide access to campus facilities, including navigation, parking and bookings. The Campus will also have an integrated medical centre offering telemedicine and emergency response services, along with dedicated wellness support. Sanjiv Bajaj, Chairman & Managing Director, Bajaj Finserv, said, “Built to global LEED and IGBC standards, the Campus will combine eco-efficient and biophilic designs with AI-driven systems and operate entirely on renewable energy. The Campus will be a testament to a tech-ready future and to India’s growing financial and technological strength.”
